parsed.explanation: State law is comparatively protective: no facilities ban, 2013 public-accommodations/employment/housing anti-discrimination act and hate-crime enhancement. Combined regime is governed at border and in federal facilities/custody by federal rules: passport sex binary, entry refusal on document discrepancy with possible permanent fraud ineligibility, ban on gender-identity-congruent federal single-sex facilities, airport screening outing, and birth-sex custody/conversion-therapy and immigration-custody abuse if detained. State protections do not cancel federal exposure. Likely outcome for outed visitor is secondary screening, entry refusal, federal-facility exclusion or humiliation, with imprisonment unlikely absent detention, but custody consequences are severe.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport binary; cable directs refusal where documents/records discrepancy or doubt on sex, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility if wilful misrepresentation suspected. Foreign advisories and stranded travellers documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; litigation ongoing. State marker change on provider statement is resident-facing climate only.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport mismatch becomes federal entry discrepancy regardless of state anti-discrimination law; no documented pre-emption or immunity from state law.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 adopts conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric therapy/drugs; stopped reporting trans prisoners. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse reported for trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for federal custody; state inmate name-change law 2015 is resident-facing.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State non-targeting lowers arrest probability, but if federal/state detention occurs, placement and care follow national regime, not state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State itself has no bathroom/facilities ban per map; 4 states criminalise in certain circumstances but this state is not listed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State 2013 act prohibits gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; July 2026 assessment places state in low-risk, non-targeting group.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodations protection operates for state/private facilities; federal buildings/funding remain under federal ban - combined traveller faces split regime.

care_services.exposure: Airport screening can out trans travellers via secondary screening/pat-downs. National orders target gender-affirming care for minors and proposed insurance bar under 18; several orders enjoined, status uncertain.
care_services.protection: State prohibits gender-identity discrimination in insurance since 2016; no state care ban for visiting adults documented.
care_services.interaction: Routine adult care in state that can continue; emergency/ward placement in federal facilities or if detained follows birth-sex regime. Minor care faces federal hostility despite state protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing as hostile/pro-trans extremism, cash-reward anti-terror guidance using 'radical gender ideology', investigation/prosecution directives re schools and minors' social transition. 66% poll support assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state enhancement since 2013; 2022 marriage recognition and 2020 employment ruling remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises outing/detention discretion at federal encounters; state hate-crime enhancement provides recourse only if state law enforcement/courts act - no enforcement data documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders direct investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating trans minor social transition, ban sports entry, and target minor care; travelling parent/minor could face school, sports or care scrutiny at federal level.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy for minors (2018 discipline, child-welfare bar) and prohibits insurance discrimination; no state facilities ban affecting family use documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: State minor protection does not cancel federal school/care/funding directives; visitor minor not resident-enrolled, so exposure is via federal facilities, care access and public events, status uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence figures or enforcement data documented; national bias incidents 1/7-1/5 of single-bias hate incidents. Poll shows majority support restrictive document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalty enhancement since 2013 and public-accommodations act; LGBTQ+ commission created Jan 2025.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State recourse is documented on paper but not shown operating for visitors; federal custody/police abuse record undermines assumption of protection if detained.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; several orders enjoined - practical exposure depends on timing. Panic-defence bill passed 2023 with no recorded signature/veto; X licence status only as of Apr 2020.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have checked some orders; civil-liberties suit on passports pending; state commission and anti-discrimination act provide complaint routes in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation creates uncertainty at entry/facilities; state remedy does not remedy federal refusal, fraud finding, or federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: extended secondary screening on document divergence, discretionary refusal of admission, slow appeal. Case is higher than pure 0.55-B because state has no facilities ban and operative anti-discrimination/hate-crime law, but lower on custody severity.

Similar: ward/facility assignment by document sex marker causing delayed/denied public services in federal settings, with uneven remedies. State facilities are protective, so exposure is federal-only, making it slightly above this anchor.

Lower: 0.75-C has brief detention, respectful inspection training, and tribunal compensation. Here entry refusal can be permanent-fraud-considered, federal facilities are banned, and documented federal custody abuse/conversion therapy creates tier-1 severity absent in 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: state layer refrains from targeting and offers public-accommodations and hate-crime protections, lowering everyday street/facility risk in state/private spaces. Federal layer creates universal exposures - binary passport enforcement, discrepancy-based entry refusal, federal single-sex facility ban, screening outing - and severe custody consequences if detained. Those federal exposures are not cancelled by state law and govern the sharpest traveller moments. No credible execution or routine imprisonment for mere presence in this state, but entry exclusion, humiliation and, conditional on detention, birth-sex custody with reported abuse pull score to elevated/reduced-risk boundary.
